d: Git tracks every change in your codebase. It's not optional — every team uses it. Understanding branching strategies, merge vs rebase, resolving conflicts, and pull request workflows is essential for professional collaboration.
c: git init clone add commit push pull

p: Git is a distributed version control system. It tracks changes to files over time using a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) of commits. It enables multiple developers to collaborate without overwriting each other's work.
2. `git add` to move to Staging Area.
3. `git commit` to save to Local Repo.
4. `git push` to upload to Remote Repo (GitHub).

# Create and switch to new branch
git checkout -b feature/auth

# Interactively rebase the last 3 commits
git rebase -i HEAD~3
